{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France#Alsace|Alsatian recipes]]

'''Flammkuchen''' or '''''tarte flambée''''' is a well-known Alsacian speciality. It is like pizza in that a thin crust of dough is baked in a very hot oven, but its topping is primarily crème fraîche, onions, and bacon. Like many traditional regional dishes there are innumerable ways of preparing it. Here is one example.

==Ingredients==
===Starter===
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] all-purpose [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|flour]]
* ¼ cup moderately hot water, about 110 °F (45 °C)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 1 package [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]

===Dough===
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] salt
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Beer|beer]] (home brew)
* 6 tbsp (¼ cup + 2 tbsp) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

===Topping===
* 2 tbsp oil
* 1 medium (3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 85 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], commercial or home made (see note)
* ½ tsp salt
* ¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinches]] [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], cut into matchsticks

==Procedure==
# Mix the starter ingredients together in a small bowl, cover tightly, and set aside in a warm place for 30 minutes.
# When the starter is light and bubbly, mix the beer and milk into the mixture.
# Put the flour and salt into a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]], then, with the motor running, add the yeast mixture through the feeding tube. Process the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] until it forms a ball. Add very small amounts of additional flour or milk if necessary.
# Process the ball until it is smooth, elastic, and warm, about 45 seconds to 1 minute.
# Butter a medium-sized bowl, roll the ball around in the butter, then cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled. Punch down and let rise a second time.
# While the dough is rising, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a nonstick [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]]. Add the onion and cook, stirring, over low heat for 5 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool.
# Combine the crème fraîche, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Add the cooled onion.
# Heat the remaining oil in the skillet and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the bacon until lightly browned, stirring constantly. Remove and drain through a strainer.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 450 °F (220 °C) or as hot as it will go. If using a [[Cookbook:Pizza Stone|pizza stone]], preheat the oven for at least 30 minutes.
# Lightly oil a 14 x 16 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (35 x 40 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]]. Roll the dough until slightly smaller than the baking sheet. Place it on the sheet. If using a pizza stone you may roll the dough onto a sheet of parchment paper.
# Spread the onion mixture over the dough, leaving a very small raised rim all the way around, then dot with the bacon.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 4 to 20 minutes depending on oven temperature. The tart should is lightly browned and bubbling. Burned/blackened edges are traditional. Serve very hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Some recipes, like the one used by restaurants in Strasbourg, do not use yeast in the dough.
* To make crème fraîche, combine 1 cup [[Cookbook:Heavy Cream|heavy cream]] with 2 tbsp cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]], stir, cover with [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]], and leave at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours, or until it has become very thick. Refrigerate, and it will become even thicker.
